title: Certified Randomness Generation against Quantum Adversaries via Energy Constraints
authors: Thomas A. Hahn, Efrat Gerchkovitz, Ester Yehuda, Rotem Arnon
abstract: For quantum random number generators (QRNGs), strong security guarantees can be obtained under various assumptions. The most well-known assumptions are the non-signalling assumption (needed for device-independent (DI) QRNG) and post-quantum computational assumptions (needed for computationally bounded single-prover QRNG protocols). In this work, we study a third model: a simple prepare-and-measure QRNG whose security relies on physically motivated energy constraints. This physically motivated set-up allows for easier implementations of QRNGs and can supply better rates.   So far, previous works that studied the energy-constrained model either assumed that the adversary is classical in their security proof or supplied relatively weak bounds on the certified randomness, by bounding the conditional min-entropy. In this work, we prove a new, essentially tight, lower bound on the single-round von Neumann entropy against adversaries holding both classical and quantum side-information. Our work reveals that working with the von Neumann entropy, rather than the min-entropy, in the quantum case can lead to a major improvement, nearly matching the classical bound in many cases. We further study the robustness of our entropy bound. Since the single-round von Neumann entropy is the main quantity of interest when characterizing the key rate of QRNGs, our bound establishes the main ingredient for rigorous security proofs against general quantum attacks in this framework.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous security analysis for Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNGs) that relies on physical energy constraints rather than abstract assumptions. By deriving a tight lower bound on the von Neumann entropy using Semidefinite Programming, the authors show a significant improvement in security guarantees compared to previous min-entropy-based methods. This establishes a key ingredient for future, practically implementable security proofs for QRNGs.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of generating certified randomness against quantum adversaries using physical constraints, specifically energy constraints, in prepare-and-measure Quantum Random Number Generators (QRNGs).
main_result: The authors derive a new, essentially tight, lower bound on the single-round von Neumann entropy against adversaries with both classical and quantum side-information. This shows that using von Neumann entropy significantly improves security bounds compared to min-entropy in this energy-constrained model.
method: The security analysis involves deriving lower bounds on the conditional von Neumann entropy using a hierarchy of Semidefinite Programs (SDPs) and advanced techniques like the Entropy Accumulation Theorem.
model_or_system: The model is a simple prepare-and-measure QRNG where security is guaranteed by bounding the energy expectation value of the prepared states ($	ext{Tr}[\mathcal{O}_\lambda ho_\lambda^x] \le \omega_x$). The adversary has access to classical and quantum side-information.
key_observables: Single-round von Neumann entropy $H(A|E, \Lambda, X=0)$, and the energy expectation values ($\omega_x$).
important_parameters: The energy bounds ($\omega_x$), the correlation parameters ($E_x$), and the structure of the side-information registers ($\Lambda, E$).
main_assumptions: The security proof relies on the energy constraint model, and the mathematical derivations involve approximations (like piecewise linear functions) and the assumption of measurement independence in certain steps.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the general adversarial model incorporating the energy constraint. Figure 2 compares the derived lower bounds on von Neumann entropy against those from min-entropy bounds as a function of the energy bound $\omega$.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the physical model and the security goal (von Neumann entropy bound). It then develops the mathematical machinery, utilizing SDPs and entropy theorems, to derive increasingly tight lower bounds on the entropy, culminating in the final SDP formulation for the bound.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, physically motivated framework for quantifying randomness security that moves beyond standard computational or non-signaling assumptions, which is highly relevant for quantum hardware implementation.
